title: The Man Whose Excessive Caution Slew Him
summary: In Damascus lived an affluent gentleman named Abu Bakr, whose terror of illness, accidents, and death grew into a ridiculous, debilitating mania. He refused to walk in the bazaa...
keywords: talk of the man whose caution slew him
full_text:
In Damascus lived an affluent gentleman named Abu Bakr, whose terror of illness, accidents, and death grew into a ridiculous, debilitating mania. He refused to walk in the bazaar for fear of falling roof-tiles; he refused to eat fruit for fear of insects; and he refused to drink water unless it had been boiled seven times and filtered through silk!

One winter, fearing that the drafty winds would give him a fatal chill, Abu Bakr constructed an airtight chamber of polished cedar inside his mansion. He sealed every window with wax, caulked every seam of the doors with felt, built a roaring charcoal furnace in the center, and shut himself within!

'Here at last,' chuckled the paranoid man, 'no draft can touch me, no cold air can reach my chest, and I am completely safe from all the perils of nature!'

However, because the chamber was completely airtight and the charcoal furnace burned without ventilation, the air was depleted of life within two hours!

When his servants finally forced open the cedar door, they found Abu Bakr lying unconscious upon his cushions, having nearly suffocated himself in his desperate attempt to avoid a common breeze!

The physician revived him with cold water and fresh air, saying: 'O Abu Bakr! Prudence is a virtue, but excessive fear is a sickness that creates the very disaster it dreads. Walk in the open sunshine, breathe the clean air, and trust the heavens, for a life lived in a box is not life at all.'
moral: Excessive, paranoid anxiety destroys life in the very effort to preserve it; live with balanced faith.
